title: Cultivating Melanized Fungi from Biological Soil Crust and Rock Surfaces
author: Tania Kurbessoian
materials: Nutrient Poor Media Glucose Asparagine Agar (GAA)

steps.title: Prepare nutrient‑poor GAA agar
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 L Glucose‑Asparagine Agar (GAA, Krainsky's Media) containing 0.500 g Dibasic Potassium Phosphate, 0.500 g (unspecified component), Asparagine 10.00 g and 15.00 g, and agar; autoclave. Add a filtered antibiotic of choice (Gentamycin, Tetracycline, Kanamycin, Streptomycin, or Chloramphenicol) to the 1 L agar solution before sterilization.

steps.title: Make sample slurry
steps.instruction: Place 0.1 g of the chosen sample (biocrust, soil, or rock surface) into a microcentrifuge tube, add 1000 µL sterile H₂O, label the tube “10⁰”, and vortex on the highest setting for 10 minutes until a slurry forms (rock samples may remain partially solid).

steps.title: Prepare serial dilutions
steps.instruction: Create three additional microcentrifuge tubes each containing 900 µL sterile H₂O and label them 10⁻¹, 10⁻², and 10⁻³. Perform a 1:10 serial dilution by transferring 100 µL of the 10⁰ slurry into the 10⁻¹ tube and vortexing, then 100 µL from 10⁻¹ into 10⁻² and vortex, and finally 100 µL from 10⁻² into 10⁻³ and vortex.

substeps.instruction: Add 900 µL sterile H₂O to each of three new tubes; label 10⁻¹, 10⁻², 10⁻³.

steps.title: Label twelve Petri plates
steps.instruction: Set out 12 empty Petri plates and label each with the date, the media name (including the antibiotic used), crust type, dilution level, and iteration (Plate 1, Plate 2, Plate 3). Prepare three plates for each dilution to provide triplicate replicates.

steps.title: Inoculate plates with dilutions
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µL of each dilution into the corresponding set of three plates: 10⁰ into the first three plates, 10⁻¹ into the next three, 10⁻² into the following three, and 10⁻³ into the final three.

steps.title: Cool agar to touchable temperature
steps.instruction: Allow the prepared GAA agar to cool to approximately 50 °C (warm enough to be handled without burning).

steps.title: Add agar to plates
steps.instruction: Pour the cooled agar slowly into the plates to avoid bubble formation, filling each plate until the agar surface closes all gaps. Process up to three plates at a time.

steps.title: Mix agar and inoculum
steps.instruction: For each set of three plates that have just received agar, gently mix the agar and the slurry by moving the plate in a careful “figure‑8” motion, ensuring even distribution without the lid touching the agar. If a lid contacts the agar, replace it with a fresh lid from an unused plate.

steps.title: Complete filling and mixing
steps.instruction: Repeat the “add agar” (step 7) and “mix” (step 8) procedures for the remaining plates until all twelve plates are filled and cooling.

steps.title: Dry and seal plates
steps.instruction: Allow the plates to air‑dry for 24 hours, then seal each plate with parafilm for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Monitor fungal growth
steps.instruction: Inspect plates over the next few days; colonies should appear on undiluted and low‑dilution plates within a couple of days, with sparser filamentous growth on higher dilutions. Melanized fungi typically become visible after 1‑2 weeks; check the underside of plates for characteristic black dots.

steps.title: Prepare nutrient‑rich MEYE agar (optional)
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 L Malt Extract‑Yeast Extract Agar (MEYE) containing 20 g malt extract, 1 g glucose, 20 g peptone, an additional 20 g malt extract, and agar (autoclave as appropriate).
